misconceptions.description: Believing that producing many storyboard versions is itself evidence of iteration, regardless of whether any change responded to a tested problem
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits five storyboard drafts but cannot name what observation drove any single change
misconceptions.feedback: Iteration evidence is a problem-change-result chain, not a version count. For each change, name the usability or load problem that triggered it.

misconceptions.description: Logging cosmetic changes (font, color, alignment) as design iterations while the underlying instructional decision never changed
misconceptions.trigger: before/after annotation shows only visual restyling but claims a learning improvement
misconceptions.feedback: Separate a polish diff from a design diff. A design diff changes what the learner must do or process; record those separately from styling.

misconceptions.description: Documenting a revision with a rationale that cites taste or instinct rather than a rubric line, tryout observation, or theory anchor
misconceptions.trigger: revision note says the change felt better with no source attached
misconceptions.feedback: Anchor each documented change to a source: a learner-tryout note, a rubric criterion, or a Mayer or cognitive-load principle.

misconceptions.description: Recording only the accepted change while omitting the alternative that was considered and rejected, so the log cannot show judgment
misconceptions.trigger: log lists final decisions only and never a discarded option
misconceptions.feedback: A defensible iteration log keeps at least one rejected alternative with the reason it lost, so a reviewer can audit the judgment.
